newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Brazil seeks common policy talks with Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks common policy talks with Argentina.

text.p: Argentina and Brazil should seek common economic policies to reduce uncertainty on the future for investors, said Sergio Amaral, spokesman of Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.

"We will have to have measures to manage macroeconomic policy, we will have to discuss more, to see where the economies are headed because economic agents need a horizon," he told La Nacion daily in an interview published Tuesday.
Amaral went on to say "there has to be a very special relationship (between Argentina and Brazil) in decision making."
But Amaral played down the disagreement. "The noises are part of the game -- there can be no such intimate or large scale process without some conflicts of interest."
"There is no need to dramatize it, because it was a localized disagreement within a much broader process, which is going very well."
Argentina and the other Mercosur partners were particularly put out by Brazil's new trade rules because they were neither consulted nor informed of them ahead of time.

Amaral said, however, that Cardoso is seeking mechanisms to prevent any repetition of this sort of dispute. "We will resolve this because we are very important partners, and because we have to have a special relationship."
The statements come just after a trade dispute was averted between Brazil and its partners in the Mercosur customs union -- Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

Brazil announced at the end of March new limits on import financing for less than 360 days, effectively forcing importers to pay in cash. Argentina led a chorus of complaints saying the new rules broke the spirit of the Mercosur.
A temporary deal was struck allowing for more flexible rules for goods entering Brazil from the Mercosur.
